newsitem.title: CANADA: Rain delays Canada Prairie harvest up to five days.
newsitem.headline: Rain delays Canada Prairie harvest up to five days.

text.p: Rainfall of up to one inch in some areas delayed Canada's Prairie harvest up to four to five days in many western regions, Pioneer Grain Co Ltd said in its crop report for the week ended Sept 4.

British Columbia's Dawson Creek region and Alberta's Peace River Valley saw violent storms scatter swathed crops and damage grain bins with up to one inch of rain falling. Swathing was stopped because of the rain, but much was done.
The rest of Alberta had harvested 50 percent of barley, 40 percent of wheat and 25 percent of canola. Yields were reported slightly below normal but quality was above average.
Fifteen percent of barley was harvested in the north with 80 percent of cereals and canola swathed.
Saskatchewan's northern grainbelt rated nine percent of crops as very good, 77 percent as good and 14 percent as fair.
Northwest Saskatchewan swathed 50 percent of cereals and 85 percent of canola. Light showers delayed harvest four to five days. About 20 percent of all crops were combined.
North central Saskatchewan lagged behind other areas with 90 percent of crops at the ripe stage. Sixty percent of cereals and 75 percent of canola was swathed with 10 percent combined.
Northeast Saskatchewan had swathed 50 percent of crops and combined 10 percent.
Southwest Saskatchewan reported 77 percent of the crop in good condition and 23 percent in fair condition.
Sixty percent of cereals were swathed with oats ahead at 80 percent. Sixty percent of flax and 90 percent of canola was swathed.
Rain and cold weather halted harvest. Harvest should be back on in four to five days.
Seventy percent of oats, 50 percent of cereals, 65 percent of canola and 40 percent of flax were combined.
Southeast Saskatchewan rated seven percent of the crop as very good, 71 percent as good and 21 percent as fair.

Seventy percent of canola, 60 percent of oats, 45 percent of cereals and 30 percent of flax were swathed. Forty five percent of canola and oats were combined, 25 percent of flax and cereals were combined.
Wheat midge was a widespread problem in wheat and durum causing light crop damage. Aphids were reported in canary seed crops south of Regina.
Eastern Saskatchewan and western Manitoba rated crops as 15 percent very good, 71 percent good and 14 percent fair.
Harvesting began and much was expected to be combined by next week if the good weather held. Yields were expected to be average.

Manitoba saw near ideal harvest conditions and swathed and combined a substantial amount of the crop. Rain on the long weekend caused some down grading of milling wheat. Reports of ergot in wheat were widespread south of Winnipeg. Yields looked average.
